properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued October 18 at 7:55AM ChST until October 19 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected for south and east facing shorelines. For the
High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves up to 30 feet
for Guam, 20 to 25 feet for Rota, and 15 to 20 feet for Tinian and
Saipan.

* WHERE...South and east facing reefs of Guam, Rota, Tinian and
Saipan.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 4 AM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low-lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will
be inundated. Shoreline erosion will occur. Breaking waves can
sweep people off their feet, and into dangerous seas. Life-
threatening swimming conditions and significant beach erosion can
be expected. Coastal inundation of 5 to 7 feet for Guam, 2 to 4
feet for Rota and 2 to 4 feet for Tinian and Saipan is possible
along with coastal flooding and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Dangerous surf from the southeast will
continue the next day or so.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay well away from the coast.

properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Monday to 4 AM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds could blow around unsecured objects and make
travel difficult. Light snow could lead to areas of blowing snow,
reducing visibility at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Following strong southerly winds north of
Trims Camp on Monday, moderate to heavy snow is expected to build
in late Monday through Wednesday as winds shift to being out of the
north. This Wind Advisory will be followed by a Winter Storm Watch
that will be in effect from late Monday through Wednesday night.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.areaDesc: Broward, FL; Palm Beach, FL
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 17 at 5:12PM EDT until October 17 at 6:45PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northern Broward County in southeastern Florida...
Southeastern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 645 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 512 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 2.5 and
5.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Coral Springs, Pompano Beach, Boca Raton, Deerfield Beach,
Margate, Lighthouse Point, Highland Beach, Coconut Creek,
Parkland, Hillsboro Beach, Boca Pointe, Godfrey Road, Boca Del
Mar, Mission Bay, Hamptons At Boca Raton, Whisper Walk, Hillsboro
Pines, Hillsboro Ranches and Sandalfoot Cove.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 645 PM EDT THIS EVENING
